title: Periodic Table Rule Breakers Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A phone runs on a lithium cell, many pressure cookers are made of aluminium, and tap water is cleaned with chlorine. Each of these elements turns up in a famous exception to the periodic trends. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 3, Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties) we find the reason behind every exception.

You will see the ionization enthalpy graph of period 2 draw itself point by point (Li 520, Be 899, B 801, C 1086, N 1402, O 1314, F 1681, Ne 2081 kJ/mol) with two dips. Orbital boxes show why: boron loses a shielded 2p electron, and oxygen loses one of a repelling pair. Next, electron gain enthalpy: chlorine (-349) beats fluorine (-328), and sulphur (-200) beats oxygen (-141), because a new electron in a small, crowded n = 2 shell feels strong repulsion. A worked example explains why boron stops at [BF4]- while aluminium reaches [AlF6]3- (4 valence orbitals vs 9), and we finish with the anomalous first members, the diagonal relationship (Li-Mg, Be-Al) and strong multiple bonds in period 2. Then the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 37 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 Three elements, three exceptions
0:32 Two dips in ionization enthalpy
1:03 Be vs B and N vs O on the bench
1:57 Pause and think: nitrogen or oxygen?
2:14 Electron gain enthalpy: Cl beats F
3:01 Worked example: [BF4]- vs [AlF6]3-
3:48 Anomalous first members and the diagonal relationship
4:20 Exam trap: more protons, higher IE?
4:50 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:21 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Chapter 4, Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure. Why do atoms bond at all, and what decides the shape of a molecule?
